svg.text: FORMAT LINEAGE: Andrew Ng, Sequoia AI Ascent (Mar 2024)
The Chart That Started 'Agentic Workflows': GPT-3.5 in a Loop Beat GPT-4 Zero-Shot (95.1% vs 67.0%)
Andrew Ng's four design patterns — two robust, two emerging — and how to get the same leap on your own task this week.
THE CHART ANDREW NG SHOWED (HUMANEVAL CODING BENCHMARK, MAR 2024)
same GPT-3.5, wrapped in an agentic loop
HumanEval (coding) as reported in the talk; the loop = reflection + tool use + planning around the same weaker model.
loop until the evaluator says 'meets the bar' (or max rounds)
Ask the model to critique its own output, then revise.
Try: 'Check this for bugs; then fix them.'
Let the model call search, code execution, calendars — it
Try: give it one tool and a verifier.
The model decomposes a goal into steps and sequences tools
Try: plan first, then execute step by step.
role-play agents debate & hand off (ChatDev, AutoGen)
Role-play agents (coder, reviewer, tester) hand work to each
other. Works best with typed handoffs.
Try: one writer, one critic, shared blackboard.
WHAT NG ACTUALLY SAID (PARAPHRASED FROM THE TALK)
Agentic workflows will drive massive AI progress this year —
possibly more than the next generation of foundation models.
Be patient: a slower agentic loop that returns a better answer in
minutes beats an instant wrong answer.
Fast token generation matters more than you think — agents read
HOW TO GET THE SAME LEAP ON YOUR TASK THIS WEEK
Pick one task with a checkable result (tests,
Add one tool that removes guessing (search or
Measure pass rate on 30 examples before and
after; keep what moved the number.
Ng's point in one line: the loop around the model is where the next 2x lives — and it is available to you today.
